top_story: By 21 September, Gaza’s war had hardened into a social catastrophe, with displaced families still living in tents and pregnant women facing childbirth after repeated bereavement and bombardment. In Jerusalem the same day, Netanyahu’s appearance in tunnels beneath Al-Aqsa and Ben Gvir’s escorted entry to the compound sharpened a deliberate assertion of control at one of the region’s most combustible sites, increasing the risk that religious symbolism will spill into wider unrest. A day earlier, Iran’s claim that Washington may resume bombing, alongside Houthi attacks on Riyadh and renewed threat rhetoric, had already pushed regional governments to brace for escalation. Together these developments show a region where civilian fragility is deepening as political and military actors raise pressure on highly sensitive fronts with little sign of restraint.
